result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=with, B=without): Both answers rank the card message clearly highest, keep it non-blocking, give it a single 'Update card' button and treat the other two messages differently from each other. B is the more complete handoff: it gives each message an ID, stores dismissals server-side, turns the warning red as the deadline nears, adds a follow-up email and lists open questions. B's date note is wrong, though (today is 15 October, not 7 October), and its '12 days' example doesn't match a 14 March deadline. A also leaves the announcement's placement vague and labels the card message 'Primary (blocking)', which is confusing. | pass 2 (A=without, B=with): Both answers make the declined-card banner the loudest, non-blocking message with an 'Update card' action. Both also give the announcement and the tip different, quieter treatments. A gets the edge because it says outright that the banner must not block the screen, uses a countdown that tightens as the deadline nears, and adds useful handoff detail like email follow-ups and message IDs. A does state the wrong current date. B is tight and clear, but it labels the banner 'Primary (blocking)', which is confusing, and it gives the deadline less weight as the reason the card message ranks first.
